arithmetic.label: Arithmetic
arithmetic.summary: Core arithmetic topics: the largest share of Tier 1 and Tier 2 Quant.

number-system.label: Number system
number-system.summary: Divisibility, remainders, unit digit, factors, number of zeros.

simplification.label: Simplification & BODMAS
simplification.summary: BODMAS, approximation, fractions and decimals, square and cube roots.

hcf-lcm.label: HCF & LCM
hcf-lcm.summary: HCF, LCM, their product rule, and word problems on both.

percentage.label: Percentage
percentage.summary: Percentage change, successive change, population and consumption.

ratio-proportion.label: Ratio & proportion
ratio-proportion.summary: Ratio, proportion, variation, and dividing a quantity in a ratio.

average.label: Average
average.summary: Average of groups, change in average, weighted average.

profit-loss.label: Profit, loss & discount
profit-loss.summary: Profit and loss, marked price, successive discount, false weights.

si-ci.label: Simple & compound interest
si-ci.summary: SI, CI, difference between CI and SI, instalments.

time-work.label: Time & work
time-work.summary: Work efficiency, alternate days, wages, pipes and cisterns.

tsd.label: Time, speed & distance
tsd.summary: Average speed, relative speed, trains, boats and streams, races.

mixture-alligation.label: Mixture & alligation
mixture-alligation.summary: Alligation rule, replacement of mixture, mean price.

partnership.label: Partnership
partnership.summary: Profit sharing by investment and time.

ages.label: Ages
ages.summary: Age problems based on ratios and sums.

algebra.label: Algebra
algebra.summary: Identities, equations, inequalities, surds and indices.

algebraic-identities.label: Algebraic identities
algebraic-identities.summary: Square and cube identities, x + 1/x type problems.

linear-equations.label: Linear equations
linear-equations.summary: Pairs of linear equations and their conditions.

quadratic-equations.label: Quadratic equations
quadratic-equations.summary: Roots, sum and product of roots, nature of roots.

surds-indices.label: Surds & indices
surds-indices.summary: Laws of indices, rationalising, comparing surds.

inequalities.label: Inequalities & maxima/minima
inequalities.summary: Basic inequalities and finding least or greatest values.

geometry.label: Geometry
geometry.summary: Lines, triangles, circles and polygons: heavy in Tier 1 and Tier 2.

triangles.label: Triangles
triangles.summary: Congruence, similarity, centres of a triangle, theorems.

circles.label: Circles
circles.summary: Chords, tangents, angle properties, common tangents.

polygons.label: Quadrilaterals & polygons
polygons.summary: Properties of quadrilaterals and regular polygons.

mensuration.label: Mensuration
mensuration.summary: Areas, perimeters, surface areas and volumes.

mensuration-2d.label: Mensuration 2D
mensuration-2d.summary: Area and perimeter of triangles, quadrilaterals and circles.

mensuration-3d.label: Mensuration 3D
mensuration-3d.summary: Cube, cuboid, cylinder, cone, sphere, frustum.

trigonometry.label: Trigonometry
trigonometry.summary: Ratios, identities and heights and distances.

data-interpretation.label: Data interpretation
data-interpretation.summary: Tables, bar graphs, line graphs, pie charts.

statistics.label: Statistics
statistics.summary: Mean, median, mode, and Tier 2 statistics topics.

c-ai-cubes.label: Cubes of big numbers
c-ai-cubes.summary: Add and subtract cubes of two-digit numbers without a calculator: last digit first, then a rough size.

c-ai-reciprocal.label: x + 1/x and its powers
c-ai-reciprocal.summary: One value of x + 1/x unlocks x² + 1/x² and x³ + 1/x³ through two small identities.

q-ai-cubes.label: Sum and difference of big cubes
q-ai-cubes.summary: Cubes of numbers like 32, 19 and 38 added, subtracted and adjusted.

q-ai-reciprocal.label: Value of x + 1/x
q-ai-reciprocal.summary: x is given (often a surd); find x + 1/x or a power of it.

q-ai-recip-power.label: A bigger expression in x, rewritten using x + 1/x
q-ai-recip-power.summary: A degree-4 (or higher) rational expression in x; divide through by the right power of x to land back on x + 1/x.

c-ai-operator.label: A symbol defined by its own rule
c-ai-operator.summary: *, ⊕, ⊗ and similar symbols are defined by a stated rule; substitute the two numbers exactly as given, in order.

q-ai-operator.label: Evaluate a custom operator
q-ai-operator.summary: A rule like a * b = 2a − 3b + ab is given; evaluate it for stated numbers, in the order the rule names them.

c-ai-zerosq.label: A sum of squares equal to zero
c-ai-zerosq.summary: Complete the square on each variable; a sum of real squares is zero only when every square is, which pins down each variable.

q-ai-zerosq.label: Pin down variables from a sum-of-squares equation
q-ai-zerosq.summary: One equation mixes squares and linear terms; rewrite it as a sum of squares equal to 0 to find every variable at once.

c-ai-symmetric.label: a + b + c = 0 and symmetric functions
c-ai-symmetric.summary: When a + b + c = 0, a³+b³+c³ = 3abc and a²+b²+c² = −2(ab+bc+ca); more generally a³+b³+c³−3abc = (a+b+c)(a²+b²+c²−ab−bc−ca).

q-ai-symmetric.label: An expression that collapses to a constant when a + b + c = 0
q-ai-symmetric.summary: a + b + c = 0 (or three quantities built to sum to 0) is given; the asked expression is always the same number, whatever a, b, c are.

q-ai-symfunc.label: Build a³+b³+c³ from the sum and the pair-sum
q-ai-symfunc.summary: a+b+c, ab+bc+ca (or a²+b²+c²) and sometimes abc are given directly; combine the identities to reach a³+b³+c³ or similar.

c-ai-polynomial.label: Polynomials: factors, remainders and roots
c-ai-polynomial.summary: p(k) = 0 exactly when (x − k) is a factor of p(x); otherwise p(k) is the remainder on dividing by (x − k).

q-ai-polynomial.label: Use p(k) to find an unknown coefficient or a root sum
q-ai-polynomial.summary: Two polynomials share a factor or a remainder at the same x = k, or roots of a quadratic are named inside the quadratic itself.

c-ai-minmax.label: Extreme value of an expression under one constraint
c-ai-minmax.summary: For a fixed sum, a sum of squares is smallest when every part is equal; a factored inequality can have an exact boundary value as its extreme.

q-ai-minmax.label: Find the greatest or least value an expression can take
q-ai-minmax.summary: 'Minimum value of a²+b²+c²' given a+b+c, or the smallest x satisfying a factored cubic inequality.

c-av-total.label: Average is total ÷ count: work with totals
c-av-total.summary: Turn every average into a total (average × count). Missing parts are then plain subtraction.

c-av-weighted.label: Weighted average
c-av-weighted.summary: Groups of different sizes: weigh each group's average by its size.

c-av-spaced.label: Evenly spaced numbers
c-av-spaced.summary: For numbers in steps (multiples of 13, odd numbers…) the average is the middle: (first + last) ÷ 2.

q-av-parts.label: Find a missing number or a group's average
q-av-parts.summary: Overall average, some group averages known; find the number or the average that is left.

q-av-weighted.label: Average of groups in a ratio
q-av-weighted.summary: Group averages and a ratio of group sizes; find the overall average.

q-av-spaced.label: Average of multiples between two numbers
q-av-spaced.summary: All integers between two limits that are divisible by k.

q-av-backsolve.label: Find a group's size or % from a combined average
q-av-backsolve.summary: Given two group averages and the combined average, find the ratio of group sizes (or a percentage split) — the weighted-average formula run backwards.

c-av-replace.label: A group's average changes when one member changes
c-av-replace.summary: Swapping out one member (or removing one, with no replacement) for another shifts the TOTAL by exactly (group size × change in average).

q-av-replace.label: Find the new, old, or removed member's value
q-av-replace.summary: The average rises or falls when a member is swapped out (for one or two others) or simply removed; find the value responsible.

c-av-series.label: Mean of a run of related numbers
c-av-series.summary: Natural/whole/odd numbers in a run, their squares, or an odd count of consecutive integers — each has its own quick mean formula.

q-av-series.label: Mean of the first n naturals, whole numbers, or odd numbers
q-av-series.summary: An evenly spaced run starting at a fixed point (0, 1, or the first odd number) — mean is (first + last)/2.

q-av-squares.label: Mean of the squares of the first n naturals
q-av-squares.summary: Needs the sum-of-squares formula, not the evenly-spaced-mean shortcut.

q-av-consec-mid.label: Mean of an odd count of consecutive integers
q-av-consec-mid.summary: The mean of an odd number of consecutive integers is simply the middle one.

c-av-overlap.label: Two groups that share one member
c-av-overlap.summary: 'First k of a set' and 'last k of a set' can share one member (like day 4 of a 7-day week counted in both a first-4 and a last-4 average) — adding both group totals double-counts it.

q-av-overlap.label: Find the member two groups have in common
q-av-overlap.summary: Given two overlapping groups' averages and the whole set's average, find the value of the member they share.

c-av-algebra.label: Average expressed symbolically
c-av-algebra.summary: Pure algebra facts about averages: shifting every term by a constant shifts the mean the same way; scaling every term scales the mean; deviations from the mean always sum to zero; two symbolic groups combine by adding their (symbolic) totals.

q-av-algebra.label: Average of x1…xn, or of two symbolic groups
q-av-algebra.summary: No actual numbers — work out how the average transforms under a shift, a scaling, a deviation sum, or combining two algebraically-described groups.

c-ci-tangent.label: Tangent-length and tangent-chord facts
c-ci-tangent.summary: A radius is perpendicular to the tangent at the point of contact. The tangent-chord angle equals the inscribed angle in the alternate segment.

q-ci-tangent-len.label: Length of a tangent segment via a right angle at the centre
q-ci-tangent-len.summary: Two external points and the centre form a right triangle (when the angle at the centre is given as 90°) — Pythagoras gives the distance between them.

q-ci-tangent-chord.label: Angle between a tangent and a chord
q-ci-tangent-chord.summary: The angle between a tangent and a chord drawn from the point of contact equals the inscribed angle subtended by that chord in the alternate segment.

c-ci-chord.label: Chord-chord angles and chords of concentric circles
c-ci-chord.summary: Two chords crossing inside a circle make an angle equal to half the sum of the two arcs they cut off. A chord of a bigger circle tangent to a smaller, concentric circle is split in half by the point of tangency.

q-ci-chord-angle.label: Angle where two chords intersect inside a circle
q-ci-chord-angle.summary: Given the two central angles for the arcs the chords cut off, find the angle between the chords.

q-ci-semicircle.label: A 90° inscribed angle marks a diameter
q-ci-semicircle.summary: If a chord subtends 90° at a point on the circle, that chord is a diameter — converse of the angle-in-a-semicircle theorem.

q-ci-concentric-chord.label: Chord of the outer circle tangent to the inner, concentric circle
q-ci-concentric-chord.summary: Half the chord, the inner radius and the outer radius form a right triangle — the chord is 2√(R² − r²).

q-ci-parallel-chord.label: Gap between two parallel chords
q-ci-parallel-chord.summary: Each chord's distance from the centre is √(r² − (half-chord)²); add or subtract these depending on whether the chords are on opposite or the same side.

c-di-sets.label: Reading a two-set table
c-di-sets.summary: Who knows A, who knows B, who knows both. 'Only' groups and the 'both' group must be added back before comparing.

q-di-overlap.label: Totals from 'only' and 'both' groups
q-di-overlap.summary: A table gives 'A only', 'B only', 'both' and 'neither'; find a total for one skill or a ratio of totals.

c-hl-rem.label: Remainder problems: the LCM sets the period
c-hl-rem.summary: Numbers that leave the same pattern of remainders repeat every LCM of the divisors, so find one such number and add multiples of the LCM.

q-hl-lcm-offset.label: Divisor minus remainder is the same every time
q-hl-lcm-offset.summary: Each remainder is the same amount short of (or over) its divisor, so N = LCM × k ∓ that amount.

q-hl-two-rem.label: Different remainders for different divisors
q-hl-two-rem.summary: Find the first number that fits both remainders, then step by the LCM; count or find the largest.

q-hl-common-rem.label: Every divisor leaves the same remainder
q-hl-common-rem.summary: N = LCM × k + r (the common remainder); pick k for the size asked (least, or greatest under a digit limit).

q-hl-remainder-extra.short: Remainder pattern plus one more filter
q-hl-remainder-extra.label: Common remainder (or gap), with an extra multiple condition
q-hl-remainder-extra.summary: Build the usual remainder form from the LCM first, then filter k so the result also divides evenly by one more given number.

c-hl-find-numbers.label: Recovering the two numbers from their HCF and LCM
c-hl-find-numbers.summary: HCF × LCM always equals the product of the two numbers; writing them as HCF × (a coprime pair) turns most of these into a short search.

q-hl-hcf-lcm-relation.label: Use HCF × LCM = product of the numbers
q-hl-hcf-lcm-relation.summary: Given three of {number 1, number 2, HCF, LCM}, the fourth is a single division away.

q-hl-sum-diff.label: Write the numbers as HCF × (coprime pair)
q-hl-sum-diff.summary: The numbers are HCF × a and HCF × b with a, b coprime and ab = LCM ÷ HCF; try the coprime factor pairs of that ratio until one matches the extra condition (sum, difference, product, or a range).

q-hl-ratio-numbers.label: Numbers already given in a ratio
q-hl-ratio-numbers.summary: For numbers in ratio a : b, LCM = HCF × a × b (when a, b are coprime); solve for whichever piece is missing.

c-hl-apply.label: Word problems that use the HCF or LCM directly
c-hl-apply.summary: HCF is the largest exact unit that measures several quantities or divides several numbers; LCM is when several repeating things next coincide.

q-hl-hcf-container.label: Biggest container, tile or group size that fits exactly
q-hl-hcf-container.summary: The largest size that measures or paves several quantities exactly is their HCF.

q-hl-hcf-remainder-diff.label: Greatest divisor leaving given (or equal) remainders
q-hl-hcf-remainder-diff.summary: Equal grouping is a plain HCF; a stated remainder is subtracted first; an unknown but equal remainder means taking the HCF of the pairwise differences instead.

q-hl-bells.label: Several things repeating on different periods
q-hl-bells.summary: Bells, lights, or runners that repeat on different periods next coincide after the LCM of those periods (LCM of fractions = LCM of numerators ÷ HCF of denominators).

q-hl-perfect-square.label: Smallest perfect square (or cube) divisible by given numbers
q-hl-perfect-square.summary: Take the LCM, then multiply by whichever primes still have an odd power in its factorisation, so every power becomes even.

q-hl-exact-divide.label: Least number exactly divisible by several numbers
q-hl-exact-divide.summary: The least number exactly divisible by several numbers is their LCM; some versions scale the number first, or add one more remainder condition on top.

c-hl-misc.label: Quick conceptual checks
c-hl-misc.summary: A short fact about how HCF and LCM relate, used as a trap rather than a calculation.

q-hl-never-lcm.short: LCM must be a multiple of the HCF
q-hl-never-lcm.label: Which value can never be the LCM
q-hl-never-lcm.summary: The LCM of two numbers is always an exact multiple of their HCF; an option that doesn't divide evenly by the HCF can never be the LCM.

c-le-point.label: A point lies on a line when it satisfies the equation
c-le-point.summary: Put the point's x and y into the equation. If both sides agree, the point is on the line.

q-le-point.label: Substitute a point into a line
q-le-point.summary: Find an unknown in the equation, or pick the option point that lies on the line.

c-le-system.label: Two or three lines drawn together
c-le-system.summary: Where two lines cross is the point satisfying both equations; three lines taken in pairs enclose a triangle whose area can be read from the crossing points.

q-le-system.label: Where lines meet, and the triangle they enclose
q-le-system.summary: Solve a pair of equations for their crossing point, or find the area of the triangle three lines form.

c-m2-circle.label: Circle: area, circumference and what scales
c-m2-circle.summary: Area grows as the square of the radius, circumference as the radius. Compare shapes before computing.

c-m2-ring.label: Rings and pathways (annulus)
c-m2-ring.summary: A ring is the outer circle minus the inner: π(R² − r²) = π(R − r)(R + r).

c-m2-sector.label: Sectors, arcs and central angles
c-m2-sector.summary: A sector is a fraction θ/360° of a circle; arc = rθ when θ is in radians.

q-m2-part.short: Part or ratio of a circle
q-m2-part.label: Part of a circle, or area ratio of similar circles
q-m2-part.summary: A fraction of a garden is cultivated; the ratio of areas of two circles; the part of a circumference in a turn.

q-m2-compare.label: Same wire: circle against square
q-m2-compare.summary: The same perimeter makes a circle or a square; compare the areas.

q-m2-ring.label: Area of a ring or a path around a circle
q-m2-ring.summary: Outer and inner radius given; area of the ring, or its ratio to the whole.

q-m2-sector.label: Sector angle, arc length and area
q-m2-sector.summary: Arc and radius give the angle; two sectors of one circle are compared.

c-m3-solids.label: Cone, prism and sphere: the formulas that matter
c-m3-solids.summary: A handful of formulas cover the exam: cone slant height, prism volume, sphere and cylinder volumes.

c-m3-displace.label: Immersed solid: volume in = volume of water raised
c-m3-displace.summary: A solid dropped into a vessel raises the water by exactly its own volume.

q-m3-cone.label: Slant height, radius or height of a cone
q-m3-cone.summary: Two of radius, height and slant height are known; find the third (Pythagoras).

q-m3-prism.label: Prism or cuboid volume after a change
q-m3-prism.summary: Base area and height give the volume; a height change scales it.

q-m3-displace.label: Sphere dropped into a cylinder of water
q-m3-displace.summary: Sphere volume equals cylinder volume of the water rise; solve for the radius.

c-mx-ratio.label: Mixtures of one liquid in another
c-mx-ratio.summary: Keep track of the part that does not change (the juice, or the milk-to-water balance) and let the other part move.

c-mx-cost.label: Mixing at different prices
c-mx-cost.summary: The mean price lies between the two prices. Alligation reads the ratio off the gaps to the mean.

q-mx-add.label: Add one liquid to change the ratio
q-mx-add.summary: A mixture in a ratio; add water (or juice) until another ratio is reached.

q-mx-replace.label: Remove some mixture, replace with one liquid
q-mx-replace.summary: Some mixture is taken out and replaced by pure milk; the final ratio is known.

q-mx-profit.label: Profit or loss on a mixed lot
q-mx-profit.summary: Two lots at different costs are combined and sold at one rate.

q-mx-allig.label: Ratio or quantity from a target gain
q-mx-allig.summary: A gain % on the mix fixes the mean cost; find the ratio of the two ingredients or how much of one to add.

q-mx-basic.label: How much of one ingredient is in a mixture
q-mx-basic.summary: Percent or ratio of an ingredient is given; find the quantity of the mixture or of the ingredient.

q-mx-repeat.label: Remove and replace more than once
q-mx-repeat.summary: The same fraction of the mixture is taken out and replaced again and again; the original liquid is multiplied by (1 − fraction) each time.

q-mx-vessels.label: Mixing two or more mixtures, vessels or alloys
q-mx-vessels.summary: Alloys or vessels in given ratios are mixed; find the mixing ratio for a target or the ratio in the final mixture.

c-ns-unit.label: Unit digits and cycles
c-ns-unit.summary: Only the last digit of the base matters, and its powers repeat in a short cycle (length 4 at most).

c-ns-rem.label: Remainders and divisibility
c-ns-rem.summary: Work with the remainder, not the big number: use the divisor's rule, or replace powers by their remainders.

c-ns-factors.label: Prime factorisation: factors, squares, trailing zeros
c-ns-factors.summary: Write the number as a product of prime powers; factor counts, perfect-square divisors and zeros all read off the exponents.

c-ns-count.label: Counting numbers in a range
c-ns-count.summary: Find the first and last member of the list, then (last − first) ÷ step + 1.

c-ns-word.label: Number word problems and digit puzzles
c-ns-word.summary: Translate the words to an equation (or to a product of digits) and solve; many are quicker by trying the options.

c-ns-series.label: Series and sums of numbers
c-ns-series.summary: Pair terms, split into APs, or use the standard sums of 1…n, squares and cubes.

q-ns-unit-pow.label: Unit digit of powers and their products
q-ns-unit-pow.summary: A product or sum of big powers; the unit digit is asked.

q-ns-unit-seq.short: Unit digit of a sum or factorial
q-ns-unit-seq.label: Unit digit of a sum or factorial
q-ns-unit-seq.summary: A sum like 1 + 2 + … + n, or n!, with the unit digit asked.

q-ns-rem-chain.label: Remainders when divided successively
q-ns-rem-chain.summary: A number divided first by one divisor and then its quotient by the next; remainders are given or asked.

q-ns-rem-large.label: Remainder of a very large number or sum of powers
q-ns-rem-large.summary: A long number, a sum of powers or a prime, divided by a small number.

q-ns-nearest.label: Least or nearest number divisible by a given number
q-ns-nearest.summary: Least n-digit number divisible by k, or the multiple of k nearest to a given number.

q-ns-div-rule.label: What must a number or expression be divisible by
q-ns-div-rule.summary: A digit-sum difference, or a sum of two big powers, and the divisors it always has.

q-ns-factors.label: Count factors, square divisors or find the largest prime factor
q-ns-factors.summary: Factorise an expression, then count with (power + 1) or find its biggest prime.

q-ns-zeros.label: Number of zeros at the end of a product
q-ns-zeros.summary: Count the pairs of 2 and 5 in a product of numbers or powers.

q-ns-count.label: How many numbers satisfy a digit or remainder condition
q-ns-count.summary: Numbers ending in a digit, leaving a remainder, or between two roots.

q-ns-word.label: Number word problems (consecutive, sum and difference, primes)
q-ns-word.summary: Consecutive odd numbers, fractions of groups, sum and difference of squares, a rational between two fractions, primes that add up to a total.

q-ns-digit-puzzle.label: Digit puzzles: repeating decimals and digit products
q-ns-digit-puzzle.summary: xy ÷ ab = 0.xyxy…, or digits of a product that follow a rule.

q-ns-series.label: Sum of a series or of the digits of a sum
q-ns-series.summary: Alternating pairs, two interleaved APs, 5 + 55 + 555…, a sum of cubes, a geometric-looking decimal series.

c-ns-frac.label: Fractions, decimals and parts of a number
c-ns-frac.summary: Compare fractions, take a part of a number, and handle 'exceeds by' and 'mistaken for' problems with one equation.

q-ns-fraction.label: Compare, order and simplify fractions and decimals
q-ns-fraction.summary: Cross-multiply or use decimals to compare; 'of' means multiply; decimals shift with powers of ten.

q-ns-parts.label: Part of a number: exceeds by, mistaken for, whole from a part
q-ns-parts.summary: Turn the story into x × (fraction − fraction) = difference, then solve for x.

c-capital-time.label: Profit shares follow capital × time
c-capital-time.summary: The one idea behind almost every partnership question.

c-late-entry.label: Late entry and changing capital
c-late-entry.summary: Partners who join late, leave early or change their capital.

c-working-partner.label: Working partner's extra share
c-working-partner.summary: A commission or salary comes off the top before the ratio split.

c-common-unit.label: Rent shared by animals: one common unit
c-common-unit.summary: Pasture and rent questions are partnership with animals instead of money.

q-pt-two.label: Two partners: share or total profit
q-pt-two.summary: Capitals and times given; find a share, or find the total profit from a share.

q-pt-late.label: Partners join at different times
q-pt-late.summary: Two or three partners; some join after some months.

q-pt-working.label: One partner works for extra %
q-pt-working.summary: A working partner takes a % of profit first, then shares the rest.

q-pt-pasture.label: Pasture / rent with animal equivalence
q-pt-pasture.summary: Different animals for different months; convert to one animal, then split rent.

c-pc-of.label: Percent of a quantity, in money and distance
c-pc-of.summary: A percent is a fraction of 100. Turn each percent into a small fraction first and the arithmetic usually cancels.

c-pc-change.label: Percentage change
c-pc-change.summary: A change of x% is a multiplier of (1 + x/100). Chain multipliers; weight them by size when parts differ.

q-pc-calc.label: Sum of percentages of quantities
q-pc-calc.summary: Several percents of several amounts, added; or commissions on items sold.

q-pc-money.label: Percent in a money story
q-pc-money.summary: A return, a price rise or a running cost; find the monthly rent or the extra expenditure.

q-pc-area.label: Percentage change of an area
q-pc-area.summary: A length changes by x%; the area changes by (1 + x)² − 1.

q-pc-mix.label: Overall change when parts change differently
q-pc-mix.summary: Spending in a ratio; each part rises or falls by its own %; find the overall change.

c-pc-use.label: Percent in exams, income, votes and mixtures
c-pc-use.summary: The story gives percents of one whole. Work on a base of 100 (or the total), keep what does not change fixed, and add or subtract the percents.

q-pc-basic.label: Percent equations: 'x% of A = y% of B'
q-pc-basic.summary: Two percents of two numbers are equal, or a number is x% of another; find the ratio or the percent.

q-pc-compare.label: A is x% more than B; how much is B less than A?
q-pc-compare.summary: Chains such as A is 40% more than B and B is 20% less than C; the reverse comparison; a number reduced and increased.

q-pc-price.label: Price change, consumption, expenditure and revenue
q-pc-price.summary: Price rises or falls and the quantity bought changes; successive changes; 'buys more for the same money'.

q-pc-growth.label: Population growth and depreciation
q-pc-growth.summary: A yearly rate applied n times, forwards (grows to) or backwards (was); a rate found from two values.

q-pc-sets.label: Pass marks, pass and fail in two subjects
q-pc-sets.summary: Pass mark found from a shortfall; passed in one subject, in the other, in both; the percent who failed.

q-pc-income.label: Spending, savings and what is left
q-pc-income.summary: A person spends parts of his income in turn; find the income, the savings, or how the savings change when income and spending change.

q-pc-election.label: Votes polled, majority and non-voters
q-pc-election.summary: Two candidates share the valid votes; the margin is the difference of their percents.

q-pc-solution.label: Percent of a substance in a mixture
q-pc-solution.summary: Water, milk, sugar, copper: add or remove one part and find the new quantity; mix two strengths.

q-pc-groups.label: Percent of groups added to give a total
q-pc-groups.summary: Boys and girls, men and women, sections of a class, each with its own percent; find the overall percent or the total.

c-pg-angles.label: Angle sum of a polygon
c-pg-angles.summary: The angles of a quadrilateral add to 360°. In a cyclic quadrilateral opposite angles add to 180°.

q-pg-ratio.label: Angles in a given ratio
q-pg-ratio.summary: Four angles in a ratio like 1 : 3 : 4 : 4; find the largest or smallest.

c-pg-regular.label: Interior/exterior angles of a regular polygon
c-pg-regular.summary: Every exterior angle of a regular n-gon is 360°/n, and it pairs with its interior angle to 180°. The angle sum is (n−2)×180°.

q-pg-sides.label: Find n from an angle condition
q-pg-sides.summary: Given a ratio, a sum, or an interior-angle value for a regular polygon, find (or rule out) the number of sides.

c-pg-cyclic.label: Cyclic quadrilateral and trapezium facts
c-pg-cyclic.summary: A cyclic trapezium is always an isosceles trapezium, so its base angles are equal. An exterior angle of any cyclic quadrilateral equals the interior angle at the opposite vertex.

q-pg-cyclic.label: Cyclic trapezium base angles, or the exterior-angle rule
q-pg-cyclic.summary: Find a base angle of a cyclic trapezium, or the interior opposite angle from a given exterior angle.

c-pg-rhombus.label: Angles and diagonals of a rhombus
c-pg-rhombus.summary: Opposite angles of a rhombus are equal and adjacent angles are supplementary. A diagonal splits it into two triangles with two equal sides (the rhombus's sides), solvable with the cosine rule.

q-pg-rhombus.label: Find a rhombus angle or diagonal
q-pg-rhombus.summary: Given one angle (or a ratio of two angles), find another angle or a diagonal's length.

c-pl-multiplier.label: Everything is a multiplier
c-pl-multiplier.summary: A profit, a loss, a markup and a discount are all just numbers you multiply the cost by.

c-pl-quantity.label: Quantity changes: false weight and free units
c-pl-quantity.summary: The seller changes how much you get, not what you pay.

c-pl-rate.label: Rates (n for ₹x) and mixing
c-pl-rate.summary: Buying and selling rates given as 'n for ₹x', or goods mixed before selling.

c-pl-symmetry.label: Equal profit and equal loss
c-pl-symmetry.summary: When two selling prices give the same profit and loss, the cost sits exactly between them.

q-pl-chain.label: Markup, discount and profit chain
q-pl-chain.summary: Marked price above cost, one or more discounts, then profit % or cost price.

q-pl-weight.label: Dishonest dealer: false weight
q-pl-weight.summary: A weight lighter than claimed, often with a markup or a discount on top.

q-pl-free.label: Free units, donation and overall gain
q-pl-free.summary: Buy n get f free, units given away, then the overall profit or loss.

q-pl-rate.label: Rates 'n for ₹x' and mixed goods
q-pl-rate.summary: Costs and selling price given as 'n for ₹x'; mix several kinds before selling.

q-pl-equal.label: Same profit and loss at two prices
q-pl-equal.summary: Profit at one price equals loss at another; find cost, or the result at a third price.

c-pl-basic.label: Cost, selling price and gain: the basic relations
c-pl-basic.summary: The one-step and two-step relations every other profit and loss question is built from.

q-pl-basic.label: Cost, selling price, profit and loss
q-pl-basic.summary: Find the cost, selling price, profit % or loss % from the figures given, including overheads and damaged goods.

q-pl-swap.short: CP of n = SP of m
q-pl-swap.label: Cost of n articles equals selling price of m
q-pl-swap.summary: Cost of one number of articles equals the selling price of another number.

q-pl-ratio.label: Ratio of cost to selling price
q-pl-ratio.summary: CP : SP is given, or SP is a multiple or fraction of CP; find the profit % or the other ratio.

q-pl-reprice.label: Selling price for a new profit or loss
q-pl-reprice.summary: A profit or loss is given at one price; find the price that gives a different profit.

q-pl-difference.label: A change of ₹d moves the result from loss to gain
q-pl-difference.summary: Sold for ₹d more, the loss becomes a gain (or the gain gets bigger); find the cost.

q-pl-profit-in-articles.label: Profit or loss equal to the price of some articles
q-pl-profit-in-articles.summary: The profit (or loss) on a lot equals the cost or selling price of a few articles.

q-pl-partial.short: Part at a gain, part at a loss
q-pl-partial.label: Parts of a stock sold at different profits
q-pl-partial.summary: A fraction of the stock sold at one rate and the rest at another; find the overall result or the total value.

q-pl-profit-on-sp.label: Profit as a percent of the selling price
q-pl-profit-on-sp.summary: Profit is quoted on the selling price, or the cost is given as a fraction of the selling price.

q-pl-sellers.label: Goods passing through several sellers
q-pl-sellers.summary: A sells to B, B sells to C, each at a profit or loss; find any one price or percent.

q-pl-successive.label: Successive discounts and the single equal discount
q-pl-successive.summary: Two or three discounts one after another, or the single discount that equals them.

q-pl-quantity.label: Price changes and the quantity bought
q-pl-quantity.summary: A price changes and the quantity or the spend changes with it; find the new rate or the percent change.

q-pl-marked.label: Find the marked or list price
q-pl-marked.summary: The selling price, a profit target or a saving is given, and the marked (list) price is asked.

q-pl-discount-rate.label: Find the rate of discount
q-pl-discount-rate.summary: Marked price and selling price (or a profit) are known; find the discount %, or the second of two discounts.

q-pl-commission.label: Commission and bonus on sales
q-pl-commission.summary: Earnings made of a % commission on sales plus a bonus on part of them.

q-pl-true-discount.label: True discount and banker's discount
q-pl-true-discount.summary: Discount on a sum due after some time at simple interest.

c-rp-change.label: Ratios after something is added
c-rp-change.summary: Write the old quantities as ratio × k (the unknown multiplier), apply the change, and match the new ratio.

c-rp-equal.label: Several quantities tied by percentages
c-rp-equal.summary: 40% of P = 0.5 of Q = 1/8 of R: set them all equal to one number k and read off the ratio.

q-rp-add.label: Ratio changes after adding
q-rp-add.summary: Quantities in a ratio; some are added and the ratio changes; find a number added or the original total.

q-rp-swap.label: Numbers and prices swapped
q-rp-swap.summary: A price ratio and a bill that changes by a % when the quantities are interchanged.

q-rp-chain.label: P : Q : R from percentage links
q-rp-chain.summary: Percentages or fractions of three quantities are equal; find their ratio.

q-rp-age.label: Ages in a ratio, now and later
q-rp-age.summary: Ages are in a ratio now; after or before some years the ratio changes; find a present age.

c-rp-basic.label: Reading, linking and combining ratios
c-rp-basic.summary: Write the quantities as ratio × k; join A : B and B : C by making the common term equal; plug in numbers for expression questions.

q-rp-basic.label: A : B : C chains, expressions and equations
q-rp-basic.summary: Join two ratios into one, find a value of x : y expressions, reciprocal ratios, equal-fraction chains and ratio equations.

c-rp-share.label: Dividing a sum and money in a ratio
c-rp-share.summary: Divide a total in a ratio, find a part from a difference, handle coins by value and incomes against expenditure.

q-rp-share.label: Divide a sum among two or more people
q-rp-share.summary: A total or a difference of two shares is given; find a share, a total or the ratio of the shares.

q-rp-group.label: Coins by value, income against expenditure
q-rp-group.summary: Coins whose values or numbers are in a ratio; savings from incomes and expenditures in ratios; averages by ratio of groups.

c-rp-prop.label: Fourth, third and mean proportionals
c-rp-prop.summary: A proportion a : b :: c : d means ad = bc; continued proportion a, b, c means b² = ac.

q-rp-prop.label: Fourth, third, mean proportionals and tests
q-rp-prop.summary: Find the missing term, check whether four numbers form a proportion, or the number added to make them proportional.

c-ms-misc.label: Sets, clocks, calendars and everyday proportion
c-ms-misc.summary: Short everyday problems: union and overlap of two sets, clock hands and strikes, calendar days, and anything that scales in proportion (shadows, rates, units).

q-ms-sets.label: Union, overlap and complement
q-ms-sets.summary: n(A ∪ B) = n(A) + n(B) − n(A ∩ B); students who play neither; complement of a set in a universal set.

q-ms-clock.label: Clock hands, strikes and clocks that gain or lose
q-ms-clock.summary: Area or arc swept by the minute hand, strikes in a day, and two clocks drifting apart.

q-ms-prop.label: Rates, shadows and units that scale
q-ms-prop.summary: Temperature at a constant rate, a short ruler, a shadow, power for several machines, walk and ride times.

q-ms-count.label: Counting integers and calendar days
q-ms-count.summary: Integers between 200 and 400 that start or end in 3; the day on which the 15th falls.

c-ci-growth.label: Compound interest is repeated multiplication
c-ci-growth.summary: Each year the amount is multiplied by the same factor (1 + r/100). So times and powers move together.

c-si-line.label: Simple interest is a straight line
c-si-line.summary: Interest = P × r × t ÷ 100. With several loans at one rate, add P × t for each and divide once.

q-ci-multiple.label: How long to grow k times?
q-ci-multiple.summary: It triples in 6 years; how long to become 27 times?

q-ci-find.label: Principal or rate from two amounts
q-ci-find.summary: A sum becomes A₁ after n years and A₂ after n + 1 years; find the rate or the principal.

q-ci-fractional.label: Compound interest for years and months
q-ci-fractional.summary: 2 years 9 months with annual compounding: compound the whole years, simple interest on the rest.

q-si-two.label: Simple interest on two loans at one rate
q-si-two.summary: Two principals for different times, total interest known; find the rate.

q-si-basic.label: Basic: interest, rate, time or principal
q-si-basic.summary: Three of P, R, T and the interest are given; find the fourth. Includes day counts, equal-interest pairs and rupee-years.

q-si-multiple.label: A sum becomes k times itself
q-si-multiple.summary: Doubles in n years; find the rate or the time to become 3, 4 or 5 times. Also interest as a fraction of the sum.

q-si-difference.label: Extra interest from a higher rate
q-si-difference.summary: A rate 2% higher (or one more year) gives Rs. X more; the extra interest is a percent of the principal.

q-si-parts.label: Money split into parts at different rates
q-si-parts.summary: A sum lent in parts at different rates; find a part, a missing rate or the average rate.

q-si-amounts.label: Amounts given, find principal or rate
q-si-amounts.summary: The amount after one time and after another (or a ratio of P : A) is given; the gap between them is the interest.

q-ci-basic.label: Basic compound interest: amount, interest or sum
q-ci-basic.summary: Find the amount, the compound interest or the sum; includes changing rates by year and the matching simple interest.

q-ci-diff.label: Difference between compound and simple interest
q-ci-diff.summary: The gap between CI and SI for 2 or 3 years is known; find the sum or the rate. Also with half-yearly compounding.

q-ci-half.label: Compounded half-yearly or quarterly
q-ci-half.summary: Halve (or quarter) the rate and double (or quadruple) the number of periods; also yearly versus half-yearly and years-and-months.

q-ci-install.label: Loans repaid in equal instalments
q-ci-install.summary: A loan repaid in two equal yearly instalments: the instalments, discounted year by year, add up to the loan.

q-ci-growth.label: Population, price or value growth
q-ci-growth.summary: A value grows or falls by a fixed percent each year: multiply by (1 ± r/100) once per year.

c-sm-compare.label: Comparing and ordering fractions
c-sm-compare.summary: Put fractions against a common yardstick (a decimal, or a benchmark like 0.6) instead of finding a common denominator.

c-sm-bodmas.label: BODMAS with nested fractions
c-sm-bodmas.summary: Work from the innermost bracket outwards, keep fractions exact, and estimate first so options can be struck.

q-sm-order.label: Arrange fractions in order
q-sm-order.summary: Four fractions to put in ascending or descending order.

q-sm-bodmas.label: Evaluate nested brackets and mixed numbers
q-sm-bodmas.summary: Brackets inside brackets, mixed numbers and a division; or a very plain sum with decimals.

q-sm-decimal.label: Decimal fractions: cancel before you multiply
q-sm-decimal.summary: Products and quotients of decimals, or a series of decimal fractions that all reduce to the same value.

q-sm-roots.label: Square roots of decimal numbers
q-sm-roots.summary: Sums of √0.49, √59.29 … and statements to be judged true or false.

q-sm-harmonic.label: Series of fractions with a known partial sum
q-sm-harmonic.summary: A series like 5/6 + 5/9 + 5/12 + … written in terms of 1 + 1/2 + 1/3 + … = k.

q-sm-root-trick.label: Expression under a root that is a perfect square
q-sm-root-trick.summary: N = a² − a − (a − 1) and √N asked: rewrite as (a − 1)².

c-sy-squares.label: Perfect squares and cubes by multiplying, dividing, adding or subtracting
c-sy-squares.summary: Write the number in primes. A square needs every power even, a cube every power a multiple of 3. Add or subtract: bracket the number between two squares or cubes.

c-sy-identity.label: Decimal sums that collapse by an identity
c-sy-identity.summary: a² − b², a³ ± b³, a + b + c = 0: spot the pattern and the answer is a ± b, a + b + c or 3abc.

c-sy-word.label: Short number puzzles on squares, sums and differences
c-sy-word.summary: Two numbers with a given sum, difference, product or sum of squares; counting squares in a range; digits in a root.

q-sy-square.label: Least number to make a perfect square or cube
q-sy-square.summary: Multiply, divide, add or subtract the smallest number so that 5808, 1323, 63522 … becomes a perfect square or cube.

q-sy-identity.label: Collapse a decimal expression with an identity

q-sy-word.label: Find the numbers from a sum, product or sum of squares
q-sy-word.summary: Sum of squares 100, difference of squares 28; perfect squares between 50 and 1000; digits in √62478078.

q-sy-compare.label: Which root expression is the greatest or the true statement
q-sy-compare.summary: Pick the largest of √a − √b pairs, or decide √5 + √3 against √6 + √2.

c-sd-compare.label: Comparing surd expressions
c-sd-compare.summary: Square both sides (both positive) so the roots shrink, or compare decimals.

c-sd-conjugate.label: Conjugates and rationalising
c-sd-conjugate.summary: (a + √b)(a − √b) = a² − b removes the root. Pairs of conjugates often cancel to a clean number.

q-sd-compare.label: Which surd expression is greater?
q-sd-compare.summary: Sums of square roots on each side; decide <, > or =.

q-sd-rationalise.label: Rationalise and simplify
q-sd-rationalise.summary: Fractions with surds in the denominator, then an expression in x.

c-ix-indices.label: Laws of indices and equations in powers
c-ix-indices.summary: Write every base as a prime power, then add, subtract or multiply the exponents. Equal bases mean equal exponents.

c-ix-nested.label: Nested roots and infinite roots
c-ix-nested.summary: a + b ± 2√(ab) is a perfect square; an infinite root √(n + √(n + …)) is the positive root of x² = n + x.

c-ix-identity.label: Decimal sums that collapse by an identity
c-ix-identity.summary: Ugly decimals are a³ ± b³ over a² ∓ ab + b², or a perfect square. Spot the identity and the answer is a ± b.

q-ix-power.label: Evaluate an expression with fractional and negative powers

q-ix-eq.label: Find x (or n) from an equation in powers

q-ix-nested.label: Simplify a nested or infinite root

q-ix-identity.label: Collapse a decimal expression with an identity

c-tw-rate.label: One day's work: rate = 1 ÷ days
c-tw-rate.summary: Convert every time to a work rate and add rates when people work together.

c-tw-lcm.label: Total work as the LCM: units of work
c-tw-lcm.summary: Pick the total work as the LCM of the times; every rate becomes a whole number.

c-tw-pattern.label: People joining on a pattern or leaving midway
c-tw-pattern.summary: Work out one full cycle, count whole cycles, then finish the remainder.

q-tw-together.label: Working together for some time: fraction left
q-tw-together.summary: Add the rates, multiply by the time, subtract from 1.

q-tw-efficiency.label: Efficiency ratio against days
q-tw-efficiency.summary: Efficiency is inversely proportional to days; swap the ratio.

q-tw-leave.label: One worker or pump stops partway
q-tw-leave.summary: Work done by all, then the remainder done by the rest. Pipes and cisterns are the same.

q-tw-cycle.label: Workers join in a repeating pattern
q-tw-cycle.summary: One cycle's work, whole cycles, then a part-day.

c-tw-manday.label: Man-days: men × days (× hours) stays constant
c-tw-manday.summary: Work = people × days × hours. Convert women and children into men, then scale or split the work into stretches.

c-tw-wage.label: Wages shared in proportion to work done
c-tw-wage.summary: Money is shared by work done (rate × days), not by days alone.

q-tw-pairs.label: A + B, B + C and C + A given
q-tw-pairs.summary: Add the three pair rates and halve to get A + B + C; subtract a pair to isolate one worker.

q-tw-others.label: A takes k times as long as B and C together
q-tw-others.summary: 'k times as long as the others together' means that person does 1/(k + 1) of the combined rate.

q-tw-less.label: One worker takes d days less than another
q-tw-less.summary: 1/x + 1/(x + d) = 1/t. Try the options, or use t squared = product of the two gaps.

q-tw-hours.label: Different hours a day: work in man-hours
q-tw-hours.summary: Convert each time to total hours (days × hours a day), then use rates per hour.

q-tw-helpers.label: How many helpers to finish in a given time
q-tw-helpers.summary: Required rate minus the rate already there, divided by one helper's rate.

q-tw-undo.label: One person builds while another destroys
q-tw-undo.summary: Destroying is a negative rate: net work = builder's rate minus destroyer's rate for those days.

q-tw-alt.label: Workers take turns, one day each
q-tw-alt.summary: Work of one pair of days, count the whole pairs, then see who works next.

q-tw-manday.label: Men, women and boys on the same work
q-tw-manday.summary: Fix 1 man = × women = y boys, express everyone as men, then use man-days.

q-tw-mdh.label: Scaling men, days and hours
q-tw-mdh.summary: men × days × hours ÷ work is the same for both cases; use it to find the unknown.

q-tw-teams.label: Men join or leave, or work is split in stretches
q-tw-teams.summary: Work out how many man-days are done, subtract from the total, and divide by the new strength.

q-tw-more.label: Extra men finish the job earlier
q-tw-more.summary: Total man-days stay fixed: n × d = (n + k)(d − e).

q-tw-wage.label: Share a payment between workers
q-tw-wage.summary: Shares are in the ratio of work done: rate × days worked for each.

c-tw-pipe.label: Pipes and cisterns: filling and emptying
c-tw-pipe.summary: A filling pipe is a positive rate, an emptying pipe or a leak is a negative rate. Add the signed rates, then divide the work by the net rate.

q-pc-together.label: Two or three filling pipes together
q-pc-together.summary: Add the rates; or use product ÷ sum for two pipes.

q-pc-three.label: Filling pipes and an emptying pipe, all open
q-pc-three.summary: Net rate = fillers − drain. Check the sign: a negative net means the tank empties.

q-pc-leak.label: A leak makes the filling slower
q-pc-leak.summary: Leak rate = normal rate − rate with the leak; it empties a full tank in 1 ÷ that.

q-pc-closed.label: A pipe is opened or closed after some time
q-pc-closed.summary: Work out the part filled in each stretch, subtract from the whole, and finish at the new rate (add clock times at the end).

q-pc-alt.label: Pipes opened alternately
q-pc-alt.summary: Net work of one pair of minutes, count whole pairs, and check whether the last minute is a filling one.

q-pc-diameter.label: Pipes of different diameters
q-pc-diameter.summary: Flow is proportional to the cross-section area, so to the square of the diameter.

q-pc-volume.label: Capacity in litres, drops and fractions of a tank
q-pc-volume.summary: Turn the given litres into a fraction of the tank (or the reverse); keep every rate in one unit.

q-pc-pumps.label: Number of pumps against time
q-pc-pumps.summary: Pumps × hours × days is fixed for the same job.

q-pc-general.label: General formulas and 'faster by' questions
q-pc-general.summary: xy ÷ (y − x) for a filler and a drain; test options for 'takes d hours less' questions.

c-tr-classify.label: Acute, right or obtuse from the three sides
c-tr-classify.summary: Compare the square of the longest side with the sum of the squares of the other two — that alone tells you the triangle's angle type.

q-tr-classify.label: Decide acute / right / obtuse from three side lengths or a ratio
q-tr-classify.summary: Given three sides (or a ratio of sides), say whether the triangle is acute-, right- or obtuse-angled.

c-tr-cevian.label: Medians, bisectors and parallel-line segments
c-tr-cevian.summary: Special segments inside a triangle — medians (meeting at the centroid, split 2:1), the angle bisector (splits the opposite side in the ratio of the adjacent sides), and any line parallel to a side (cuts the other two sides in the same ratio).

q-tr-median-hyp.label: Median to the hypotenuse of a right triangle
q-tr-median-hyp.summary: The median from the right angle to the hypotenuse is always half the hypotenuse.

q-tr-equilateral-seg.label: Inradius, circumradius and median of an equilateral triangle
q-tr-equilateral-seg.summary: In an equilateral triangle these three special lengths are all fixed multiples of each other.

q-tr-median-perp.label: Two medians meeting at right angles
q-tr-median-perp.summary: Split each median 2 : 1 at the centroid, then use the right angle between them with Pythagoras.

q-tr-bisector.label: Internal bisector splitting the opposite side
q-tr-bisector.summary: An internal angle bisector splits the opposite side in the same ratio as the two adjacent sides.

q-tr-parallel.label: Basic proportionality (Thales) theorem
q-tr-parallel.summary: A line parallel to one side of a triangle cuts the other two sides proportionally — use it to find a missing segment.

c-tr-centers.label: Incentre, circumcentre and orthocentre
c-tr-centers.summary: The incentre gives a clean angle formula (∠BOC = 90° + A/2). Where the orthocentre or circumcentre sits (inside, on a vertex/side, or outside) tells you the triangle's type.

q-tr-incentre.label: ∠BOC = 90° + A/2 at the incentre
q-tr-incentre.summary: Given two angles (or the vertex angle A directly), find the angle the incentre makes with the other two vertices, or run the formula backwards.

q-tr-center-facts.label: What a centre's special position tells you
q-tr-center-facts.summary: Orthocentre = centroid ⟺ equilateral. Orthocentre on a vertex ⟺ right-angled there. Circumcentre outside ⟺ obtuse.

c-tr-angles.label: Radians and degrees
c-tr-angles.summary: π radians = 180°. Convert by replacing π with 180.

c-tr-ratios.label: Ratios of an acute angle
c-tr-ratios.summary: From one ratio get the other five with a right triangle; complementary angles swap sin and cos.

q-tr-convert.label: Convert radians to degrees
q-tr-convert.summary: An angle like 3π/2 radians in degrees.

q-tr-complement.label: sin(90° − B) = cos B
q-tr-complement.summary: A ratio of (90° − B) is given; find the cofunction of B.

q-tr-triangle.label: Another ratio from one ratio
q-tr-triangle.summary: cos A = 5/13 (A acute); find tan A.

c-sd-basic.label: Speed, distance and time: units first
c-sd-basic.summary: One formula and one habit: write minutes and hours in the same unit before dividing.

c-sd-relative.label: Relative speed: meeting and chasing
c-sd-relative.summary: Towards each other speeds add; in the same direction they subtract.

c-sd-circular.label: Overtaking on a track
c-sd-circular.summary: The faster one overtakes after closing the gap between them at the relative speed.

q-sd-convert.label: Same distance, different time or route
q-sd-convert.summary: Distance changes by a percentage, time is fixed, find the new speed.

q-sd-units.label: A rate in short time scaled to a long time
q-sd-units.summary: Distance in 1 minute; find the distance in hours.

q-sd-meet.label: Two bodies meet: opposite or same direction
q-sd-meet.summary: Two meeting times give two equations: sum and difference of speeds.

q-sd-overtake.label: First overtake on a circular track
q-sd-overtake.summary: Gap ÷ relative speed gives the time; times the faster speed gives the distance.

c-sd-train.label: Trains: crossing poles, platforms and each other
c-sd-train.summary: A train crossing something covers its own length plus that object's length at its speed; two trains use the relative speed.

c-sd-avg.label: Average speed = total distance ÷ total time
c-sd-avg.summary: Never average the speeds. Add the distances, add the times, divide.

c-sd-late.label: Changing the speed: arriving early or late
c-sd-late.summary: Speed and time are inverse; the gap between two journey times (early + late) fixes the distance.

c-sd-race.label: Races: beats by, starts and ratios of speeds
c-sd-race.summary: Convert 'beats by 100 m' into the ratio of distances run in the same time, then chain the ratios.

q-sd-basic.label: Distance, speed and time, with units and fractions
q-sd-basic.summary: One formula; turn minutes into hours, fractions of a journey into km, and keep clock times honest.

q-sd-ms.label: Converting km/h to m/s and back

q-sd-wheel.label: Wheel turns, circumference and speed
q-sd-wheel.summary: One turn covers the circumference π d; distance = turns × π d.

q-sd-ratio.label: Ratios of speeds, times and distances
q-sd-ratio.summary: Speed ∝ distance ÷ time: divide the distance ratio by the time ratio.

q-sd-angle.label: Two walkers at right angles
q-sd-angle.summary: Distances travelled are the two legs of a right triangle; use Pythagoras or the 3-4-5, 5-12-13 triples.

q-sd-chase.label: Policeman and thief, one overtakes the other
q-sd-chase.summary: Head start ÷ (faster − slower) is the time to catch up.

q-sd-relative.label: A train passing a man or vehicle that is moving
q-sd-relative.summary: Same direction: subtract the speeds; opposite: add. The train's length is covered at that speed.

q-sd-lap.label: Runners on a track meet again at the start
q-sd-lap.summary: They are together again at the start after the LCM of the lap times.

q-sd-pole.label: A train crossing a pole or a man standing
q-sd-pole.summary: Distance covered = the train's own length.

q-sd-platform.label: A train crossing a platform, bridge or standing train
q-sd-platform.summary: Distance = train + platform; the extra time over a pole crossing is the platform's time.

q-sd-trains.label: Two trains crossing each other
q-sd-trains.summary: Opposite: add the speeds; same direction: subtract; the distance is the sum of the lengths.

q-sd-average.label: Average speed over unequal stretches
q-sd-average.summary: Total distance ÷ total time; 2uv/(u + v) for equal distances.

q-sd-late.label: A change of speed makes him early or late
q-sd-late.summary: D/v1 − D/v2 = the total time gap (late + early). Test the options.

q-sd-race.label: A beats B by, start and finishing ratios
q-sd-race.summary: Distances run in the same time give the ratio of speeds; chain A : B and B : C.

c-sd-boat.label: Boat and stream: downstream and upstream
c-sd-boat.summary: With the stream the speeds add, against it they subtract; the boat and the stream are the half-sum and half-difference.

q-bs-speeds.label: Find the boat or the stream from down and up data
q-bs-speeds.summary: Downstream speed D, upstream speed U: boat = (D + U)/2, stream = (D − U)/2.

q-bs-time.label: Time taken for a given distance
q-bs-time.summary: Find the right speed (down, up or still water), then time = distance ÷ speed.

q-bs-return.label: Round trip, total time, find the distance or the boat
q-bs-return.summary: D/(x + y) + D/(x − y) = total time; test the options when the boat is wanted.

q-bs-ratio.label: Time and speed ratios: twice as long, thrice as long
q-bs-ratio.summary: Times are inverse to speeds: a 2 : 1 time ratio makes down : up = 2 : 1, boat 3 parts, stream 1 part.

q-bs-pairs.label: Two journeys with different mixes of up and down
q-bs-pairs.summary: Use hours per km for up and down; add and subtract the two equations.

q-bs-same.label: 5 km with the stream = 4 km against it
q-bs-same.summary: Same time means the speeds are in the ratio of the distances.

q-bs-flow.label: Meeting of two boats, drift and volume of flow
q-bs-flow.summary: The stream cancels when the boats go opposite ways; the volume of flow is cross-section × length moved.

A curated selection of 26 of the chapter's 440 questions: the chapter is extremely repetitive (the same 'x + 1/x' and 'a + b + c = 0' identities recur dozens of times with only the numbers changed), so two to five representative questions are kept per distinct pattern rather than every repeat. The question numbers are the book's own. Every answer was recomputed and compared with the book's printed answer key (the chapter has no separate worked-solution pages before the key, only questions then a two-page answer-key table). Split across three topics by the technique each question actually uses: most of the symbolic-identity questions go to algebraic-identities, two ratio/variation questions to ratio-proportion, and two coordinate-geometry questions to linear-equations.

Chapter 17 (book pp. 526-597, PDF pp. 529-600) has 400 geometry questions. Extremely repetitive within each sub-pattern (polygon-angle algebra, cyclic-quadrilateral/trapezium facts, rhombus angle/diagonal, triangle classification, special segments of right and equilateral triangles, the incentre/circumcentre/orthocentre family, the basic-proportionality/angle-bisector cevian family, and circle theorems: tangent length, tangent-chord angle, chord-chord angle, chords of concentric circles, parallel chords). 32 representative questions were kept (2-4 per sub-pattern) and routed to three topic files: polygons (8, extending the existing topic), and two brand-new topics, triangles (16) and circles (8), since no topic file previously covered triangle centres or circle theorems. Unlike Chapter 16, this chapter has no compact answer-key table: the book gives full worked 'Explanatory Notes' instead, and the ones located cover only roughly the chapter's last 90 questions (about Q317-400), not the earlier questions this selection draws from. So every answer here was verified the primary way only: independently recomputed from the question's own numbers (never the book's working) and checked to match exactly one of the four printed options, with no separate book-key cross-check for this chapter.

Chapter 18 (Average) starts at book p.598 (PDF p.601); its question pages run well past book p.612 (seen through at least Q221). Extremely repetitive within each sub-pattern (weighted/combined average of differently sized or ratio-weighted groups, backward-solving for a group's size/percentage from a combined average, replacement/removal changing a group's average, mean of an evenly-spaced run of numbers, mean of squares, consecutive-integer mean-is-the-middle-term, the classic 'overlapping day' average puzzle, and a cluster of pure algebraic average identities: shift by a constant, scale by a constant, sum of deviations is zero, combining two groups symbolically). 23 representative questions were kept (2-6 per sub-pattern) and filed into the existing average.py topic: two new PYQs for the pre-existing q-av-weighted and q-av-parts qtypes, plus five brand-new qtypes (q-av-backsolve, q-av-replace, q-av-series, q-av-squares, q-av-consec-mid, q-av-overlap, q-av-algebra). As with Chapter 17, no separate book answer-key table was located for the question range used here, so every answer was verified the primary way only: independently recomputed from the question's own numbers and checked to match exactly one of the four printed options.

Chapter 19 (LCM & HCF) starts at book p.644 (PDF p.647) and runs through book p.649 (145 questions total, organised by SSC exam year). This selection draws only from the first two question pages, book pp.644-645 (Q1-44): 33 representative questions were kept and filed into the existing hcf_lcm.py topic. One new PYQ (Q19) extends the pre-existing q-hl-lcm-offset qtype; everything else is new (q-hl-common-rem, q-hl-remainder-extra, q-hl-hcf-lcm-relation, q-hl-sum-diff, q-hl-ratio-numbers, q-hl-hcf-container, q-hl-hcf-remainder-diff, q-hl-bells, q-hl-perfect-square, q-hl-never-lcm, q-hl-exact-divide). Q20 (a bell-ringing question) was dropped: the independently computed meeting time did not match any of its four printed options. As with Chapters 17-18, no compact printed answer-key table was located for this question range, so every answer here was verified the primary way only: independently recomputed from the question's own numbers and checked to match exactly one printed option. Q3's Hindi text gives LCM 225 (a copy-paste slip from Q2); its English text and all four printed options are only consistent with LCM 30, which is what was used.
